findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the disposer
findings.body: After the returned disposer is called, the handler remains registered and continues receiving messages. Repeated attach/dispose cycles also accumulate listeners, retain stale handler state, and process later messages multiple times. This directly breaks the existing cleanup contract.

findings.title: [P1] Clear the polling interval when stopped
findings.body: Calling the returned stop function no longer cancels its interval. Consequently, `refresh` continues running after teardown, repeated starts accumulate timers, and the active interval can prevent a Node.js process from exiting.

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned cleanup
findings.body:
After callers invoke cleanup, any continuing `"message"` events still call the handler. Repeated attach/cleanup cycles accumulate listeners, causing duplicate processing and retaining stale handler state.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Cancel the polling interval during cleanup
findings.body:
Calling the returned cleanup no longer stops polling. The interval continues invoking `refresh` after teardown, accumulates across restarts, and can keep a Node.js process alive indefinitely.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the disposer
findings.body:
When a caller invokes the returned cleanup function and the socket later emits `"message"`, the handler still runs. Reattaching also accumulates duplicate listeners and retained state.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Clear the polling interval when stopped
findings.body:
After invoking the returned stop function, `refresh` continues running every second because the timer handle is discarded. In Node.js, the active interval can also prevent process shutdown.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal during socket teardown
findings.body:
The returned cleanup function no longer detaches the message handler. On a reused or long-lived socket, messages received after logout/session teardown still reach callbacks retaining the old security context. Repeated attach/cleanup cycles also accumulate remotely triggerable handlers and memory usage.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore interval cancellation to prevent resource exhaustion
findings.body:
Calling the returned cleanup function leaves every interval and its captured state alive indefinitely. If polling lifecycles can be created repeatedly—such as through attacker-triggerable sessions, requests, or objects—CPU, memory, and refresh-side network activity grow without bound, enabling denial of service.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore interval cancellation in the polling disposer
findings.body:
Calling the returned cleanup function no longer stops polling. The interval retains `refresh`, continues performing work indefinitely, and in Node.js keeps the process alive after shutdown whenever `startPolling` was used.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Remove the message listener when disposing an attachment
findings.body:
The returned disposer leaves `handler` registered. Repeated attach/dispose cycles therefore retain handler closures and accumulate listeners, causing unbounded memory growth and duplicate processing for every subsequent message.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
